slides.title: Two witnesses sign
slides.body: Sign your will in front of two witnesses, and both sign it too. A beneficiary should not be a witness, or their gift can fail.

slides.title: Registration is optional
slides.body: An unregistered will is valid. Registering it at the Sub-Registrar's office is optional but makes it harder to dispute. No stamp paper needed.

slides.title: Change it any time
slides.body: You can change or cancel your will while alive. The latest valid will counts. Probate is no longer compulsory, even in Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata.

caption_instagram:
Many family property disputes start with one thing: no clear will. A will is simpler to make than most people think. 📝

✍️ Write it down and sign it in front of two witnesses; both witnesses sign too (Indian Succession Act, s.63)
🚫 Don't make a beneficiary (or their spouse) a witness — the gift to them can become void (s.67)
🏛️ Registration is optional; registering at the Sub-Registrar's office makes it harder to challenge
📄 No stamp paper is needed
🔄 You can change or cancel your will any time while alive — the latest valid will counts (s.62)
⚖️ Probate is no longer compulsory, even in Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata (Repealing and Amending Act, 2025)

caption_linkedin:
Succession disputes are among the most common family litigation in India, and many begin with the absence of a clear will. The legal requirements under the Indian Succession Act, 1925 are simpler than people assume:

• Execution (s.63): the will must be signed by the testator and attested by two witnesses, each of whom has seen the testator sign
• Witnesses (s.67): a bequest to an attesting witness, or to the witness's spouse, is void — so beneficiaries should not attest
• Registration: optional under the Registration Act, 1908; a registered will is harder to dispute
• No stamp paper is required for a will
• Revocation (s.62): a will can be changed or revoked at any time during the testator's lifetime; the last valid will prevails
• Probate: following the Repealing and Amending Act, 2025, probate is no longer compulsory, including for wills made in Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata
